overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting a Dec. 2, 2024 notice that failed to name the license-renewal and New Year's Eve extension applicants and the specific license types, but not as to the permit-fee topic.

allegations.summary: Notice for the Dec. 2, 2024 meeting allegedly lacked specificity by not naming the businesses up for annual license renewal.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice where it failed to list the applicants or licensees, as well as the specific type of licenses the Board was considering.

allegations.summary: Notice allegedly lacked specificity by not naming the businesses seeking New Year's Eve hours extensions.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, the Board admits, and we find, that the notice also did not include further detail on the specific businesses that sought an extension of hours for New Year’s Eve.

allegations.summary: Topic 'Request for Permission to Waive Permit Fees – Building Department' allegedly lacked any detail to be sufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the information listed on the notice with respect to this topic was sufficient to reasonably advise the public of the matter to be discussed at the meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements (Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
